name: Silicon (1 % biaxially strained)

lattice.source: Hypothetical: bulk silicon lattice parameter scaled by 1.01 to illustrate a plug-in-supplied material. Not a measured structure.

terminations.description: Ideal bulk truncation, one dangling bond per surface atom.
Ideal bulk truncation, two dangling bonds per surface atom.
Monohydride Si(111):H-1x1, the wet-chemically prepared ideally flat surface.

reconstructions.description: Takayanagi dimer-adatom-stacking-fault reconstruction of clean Si(111).
reconstructions.reference: K. Takayanagi et al., Surf. Sci. 164 (1985) 367
reconstructions.note: Not implemented in v0.1. Requesting it returns an explicit unsupported result rather than an approximate structure.

reconstructions.description: Rows of surface dimers on the strained (100) surface, built by the same generator as unstrained silicon.
reconstructions.reference: R. E. Schlier and H. E. Farnsworth, J. Chem. Phys. 30 (1959) 917
reconstructions.note: The generator applies here because the prototype and orientation match. No reference_geometry block is given: the LEED structure determination for Si(001)-(2x1) is for the unstrained surface and would be the wrong comparison for a 1 % biaxially strained one. Materia therefore reports the computed geometry with no comparison rather than an inapplicable one.
reconstructions.method: Generator establishes the pairing; geometry comes from relaxation of this strained cell.

band_gap.source: S. M. Sze, Physics of Semiconductor Devices, 3rd ed.
band_gap.note: Copied from unstrained silicon; strain-induced band-gap changes are NOT applied.
